Treatment summary
The patient presented atfer a sideswipe collision during a lane change and reported
low back pain with muscle tightness and limited range of motion. The mechanism of
injury is consistent with the reported pain, and the presentation is plausible for a
crash of this type. Imaging and physical examination findings clearly confirm a lumbar
strain. No prior injury to the lower back is known from the history provided. Care
consisted of eleven visits, includnig manual therapy, graded therapeutic exercise, and
home program instruction. Treatment followed a typical course, with visit frequency
decreasing as pain and mobility improved. At the most recent visit the patient
reported near-resolution of symptoms and had regained functional range. Two similar
charges recorded on the same day are currently under review for accuracy. Discharge
from active care is anticipated, with a return precaution given should symptoms recur
or new neurological signs develop.

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.

- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
